label: OpenAVC logic engine
info:
A panel button sets var.request_source; this flow decides what to do about it, switches the projector's input, and writes var.status back so a label on the panel can show it. The panel never knows where the logic lives.

Matches the Conference Room starter project (device projector1, command set_input). In the UI Builder, give a button a Set Variable action: var.request_source = "laptop" (or "wireless"), and bind a label's value to var.status. The inject node at the top does the same as that button, so you can try the flow before building the panel.

The state get node reads the projector's power before switching: a projector that is off gets a status line instead of a command it cannot take.

Once it has acted, the flow clears var.request_source again, so pressing the same button twice runs the flow twice: a variable only reports a change, and the same value written twice is not one.

Point the openavc-server node at your system and deploy.

name: In the UI Builder: a button whose press does Set Variable var.request_source = "laptop", and a label bound to var.status
which input?
status line
func:
msg.payload = msg.payload.success ? `Showing ${msg.source}` : `Could not switch: ${msg.payload.error}`;
return msg;
